question: There are growing concerns that the agreement signed between the Turkish state-owned crude oil and natural gas trading company, BOTAS, and Bulgarian operator, Bulgargaz, could undermine EU energy sovereignty by giving President Erdoğan a political lever in future dealings with the EU.

The agreement will allow gas, regardless of its actual origins, to be rebranded as ‘Turkish gas’ and flow via infrastructure owned or controlled by Bulgargaz into European gas networks. In addition, there are fears that arrangements in the agreement could be economically damaging to Bulgaria.

In October 2023, nine months after concerns had been flagged to it about the agreement, the Commission announced that it was undertaking an examination of the agreement. Can the Commission indicate: 1.
When it expects to complete its examination of the agreement and indicate how much progress it has made to date?

Whether Bulgargaz has made available to it all documentation needed to complete its examination, including details of any conditions the agreement contains regarding the origins of gas that will come into the EU under the arrangements facilitated by the agreement?
Whether it will publish an interim report on the agreement before the final plenary session of the current EU Parliament?
